elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: § 21.1 as rendered: "each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed ..." followed by "The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims." Mutuality is expressed twice and was left untouched by the edit; no competing one-sided "Vendor shall not be liable" or "Customer's liability is unlimited" language appears elsewhere in the liability regime.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Amended § 21.1: "shall not exceed the greater of (a) all amounts paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000." The greater-of construction, the "paid or payable" basis, the 12-month look-back tied to the event giving rise to the claim, and the USD 1,000,000 floor are all present. Substituting "all amounts ... under this Agreement" for the defined term "Fees" is necessary and correct because § 1.5 defines "Fees" as only the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee (§ 1.6); the substitute basis is at least as large as "fees" and also removes the "first Order Form" narrowing.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: § 21.2 (unchanged): "Except for Excluded Claims, neither Party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, punitive, or consequential damages, or for lost profits, revenues, or goodwill ..." "Neither Party" makes the exclusion mutual, and the retained sentence characterising data-restoration, replacement-service, notice and incident-response costs as direct damages is favourable to us and was preserved.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: § 21.3 defines "Excluded Claims" to include "a Party's breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations", and § 21.1 opens "Except for Excluded Claims", so confidentiality breaches sit outside the cap for both parties.

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Same § 21.3 carve-out expressly names "data-protection, or security obligations" within Excluded Claims, which § 21.1 excepts from the cap.

§ 21.3 Excluded Claims includes "its indemnification obligations"; combined with the "Except for Excluded Claims" opener in § 21.1, the § 20 indemnities are not swallowed by the cap (no super-cap needed).
§ 21.3: "gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud" are Excluded Claims and therefore outside the § 21.1 cap.
§ 21.3 lists "wilful misconduct" among Excluded Claims, excepted from the cap by § 21.1 and from the damages exclusion by § 21.2.
§ 21.3 lists "fraud" among Excluded Claims, excepted from the cap by § 21.1.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: § 21.3: "infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property" is an Excluded Claim and therefore uncapped; the reciprocal "other Party's" formulation keeps it mutual.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: § 21.3 final sentence (unchanged): "Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees for conforming Services is not damages and is not limited by this Section." Note the sentence keys to the narrow § 1.5 "Fees" (Implementation Fee only), so it is under-inclusive as to recurring subscription charges — but that under-inclusion operates in Customer's favour (it leaves more of our payment exposure inside the cap), so no repair is required and none was made.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: § 21.1: "each Party's total aggregate liability ... The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims."

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: Amended § 21.1 ties limb (a) to "all amounts paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim", replacing the illusory "Fees ... under the first Order Form" basis (a one-time USD 12,000 charge under §§ 1.5–1.6) that had put the clause below the six-months walk-away line.
§ 21.3 Excluded Claims includes "its indemnification obligations"; § 21.1 excepts Excluded Claims from the cap.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: § 21.3 Excluded Claims includes "a Party's breach of confidentiality ... obligations", excepted from the cap by § 21.1.
§ 21.3 Excluded Claims includes "gross negligence", excepted from the cap by § 21.1.
§ 21.3 Excluded Claims includes "wilful misconduct", excepted from the cap by § 21.1.

reasons: The deviation call is correct on the original text: § 21.1 keyed the cap to "Fees", which § 1.5 defines as only the § 1.6 one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee "stated in the first Order Form", so the twelve-month look-back captured nothing recurring (recurring spend plainly exists — § 7.2 annual subscription Fees, § 8.3 recurring Fee increases). An effective USD 12,000 ceiling sits below six months' fees, which is express walk-away territory, so the clause failed the fallback on a material term and warranted a redline.

All eleven preferred elements are met in the rendered operative language: mutual cap (§ 21.1, stated twice), greater-of 12-months paid-or-payable plus a USD 1,000,000 floor (amended § 21.1), mutual indirect/consequential exclusion (§ 21.2), and the full Excluded Claims set in § 21.3 (confidentiality, data protection and security, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, other-party IP infringement) plus the payment-obligations sentence. The fallback is met a fortiori.

Bypassing the poisoned defined term rather than amending § 1.5 is the correct repair: broadening "Fees" globally would have inflated our own exposure under the § 7.7 liquidated-damages mechanic and § 8.3 uplift language. Confining the fix to § 21.1 leaves the rest of the fee architecture undisturbed.

Minimality holds: a single in-sentence replacement inside § 21.1, retaining the favourable "Except for Excluded Claims" opener and the mutuality sentence, with §§ 21.2 and 21.3 untouched. No operative term is duplicated and nothing outside the LOL-CAP checklist (e.g. no super-cap, no insurance or indemnity edits) was added.

Intent is preserved: the trigger (event giving rise to the claim), the 12-month timing, the direct-damages characterisation of restoration/replacement/notice/incident-response costs, and the payment-obligation carve-out all survive without contradiction; the amended limb (a) no longer collides with the narrow "Fees" definition still used in § 21.3 and elsewhere.

One deliberate trade-off worth naming to the business, not a defect: because the cap is mutual, moving limb (a) to "all amounts paid or payable" and adding the USD 1,000,000 floor also raises Customer's own ceiling. That is exactly the playbook preferred position, and our payment obligations for undisputed Fees remain outside the cap under § 21.3, so no further edit is required.

Optional (do not redline on this rule): § 21.3's payment carve-out reads on the narrow "Fees" definition, so only the Implementation Fee obligation is expressly treated as non-damages. That under-inclusion favours us and should be left alone; if Vendor asks to align it with "all amounts", resist, since it would push our recurring payment exposure outside the cap.

Margin comment is on-tone and accurate: it states the preferred position, explains why the "Fees" basis made the cap illusory, and confirms that mutuality, the damages exclusion and the Excluded Claims carve-outs are unchanged. No fallback needs to be offered because the edit lands at the preferred level.
